correctness.rationale: An admissible new-point comparison profile is a downset L and an upset U with l<u for every l in L and u in U. These conditions are necessary and suffice for transitivity and disjointness. Universality and homogeneity realize this finite extension over the pointwise named base and identify all realizations of a given profile by automorphisms. A profile isolates the corresponding complete type, and the extension can have arbitrarily many pairwise incomparable copies, so the type is nonalgebraic. Equality types are excluded. Counting one-sided profiles gives 2I−1, with I including the empty ideal, and adding b gives 2a+b+1. Ideals multiply in a parallel composition and have count I(P)+I(Q)−1 in an ordinal sum (proper ideals of P, or all P plus an ideal of Q). A two-sided profile in a parallel composition lives in just one component. In an ordinal sum, a two-sided profile internal to P forces all of Q above the new point, one internal to Q forces all of P below, and the remaining profiles are exactly a nonempty ideal of P paired with a nonempty filter of Q. These disjoint cases give the stated b recurrences. Empty and singleton leaves, arbitrary nesting, and the diamond all agree. Linear arithmetic-operation complexity is in the actual number of leaves, counting empty leaves; counts are bounded by 3 to the power of the number of vertices, which is at most the leaf count.
correctness.verification: Independent finite reproduction: enumerate downsets by subsets and label every old point below, incomparable, or above the new point, retaining profiles whose augmented strict relation is transitive and preserves the old order. For distinct orders from ordered binary expressions at sizes 1–6 the counts of orders checked were 1, 2, 6, 22, 90, 394; all matched. The empty base gave (a,b,t)=(0,0,1), the diamond (5,7,18). The frozen package supplies verify_series_parallel.py and verification_output.txt (lines 1–5); the latter counts six ideals including the empty one for the diamond. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed. Finite checks corroborate the decomposition proof, not unrestricted correctness on their own.
